scenes.heading: Building a second-shooter or associate network as you grow

sents.d: Building a second-shooter or associate network as you grow
Turning down bookings because you're already busy is a signal it might be time to build a small team.

scenes.heading: Add a second shooter when booked out

sents.d: When you're consistently turning away work or double-booked on peak dates, bringing in a second shooter or associate photographer (paid per job, not a full employee) lets you say yes to more without personally shooting every single job.
Start with someone whose style you trust and can brief clearly — a short shot list and clear expectations upfront matters more than a long trial period, especially for one-off assist work.
Be upfront with clients about who's shooting if it isn't you personally; most are fine with it as long as they know in advance and trust that you're overseeing the quality.

take: Bring in trusted associates and be upfront with clients.
